narrative:
The model estimated a 56.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That means it judged repayment difficulty to be slightly more likely than not, so your application was denied; this is not a certainty, but it was enough to fail the lending decision.

Your borrowing history was the single most important reason. The record shows no credits or all paid, a pattern found for only about 1% of approved applicants, so it was treated as a weak or unusual borrowing track record and pushed toward bad risk. Second was your checking account balance of 0–200 DM; this modest balance also pushed toward bad risk, though about 18% of approved applicants have this balance. Next, ask the lender what evidence would strengthen a future application, and consider applying for a smaller amount or building a clearer credit record. You could also provide stronger proof of income, savings, or a guarantor if available, and check your credit file for errors before reapplying.
